question: Can a learnable forward-only residual scaling control depthwise activation growth in pre-normalized transformers without shrinking backpropagated gradients, thereby improving language-model pretraining convergence?

key_findings.claim: GPAS deliberately decouples its forward mapping from its backward derivative.
key_findings.evidence: After a residual sublayer produces x', GPAS outputs x' minus SiLU(alpha) times stop-gradient(x'). Forward activations are multiplied by a learned factor, while the derivative with respect to x' remains one; gradients still update alpha through the stopped activation value.

key_findings.claim: Across 71M-1B runs, adding GPAS usually lowers perplexity for several normalization schemes.
key_findings.evidence: On C4, Pre+GPAS improves 1B evaluation perplexity from 16.92 to 16.25; LNS+GPAS improves 15.65 to 14.88, and Sandwich+GPAS has the largest 350M drop, 21.54 to 19.79. A partial 7B run at 16B tokens reports 15.27 versus 13.82.

key_findings.claim: The stop-gradient is the operative ingredient rather than activation shrinkage alone.
key_findings.evidence: At 350M, removing stop-gradient still cuts activation variance by about half but produces no meaningful perplexity improvement; alternative insertion locations all help less than scaling immediately after the residual sublayer. Fixed gates also converge substantially worse than learned gates.

key_findings.claim: GPAS can introduce its own optimization instability and relies on surrogate rather than true forward gradients.
key_findings.evidence: A gate spike near step 10K temporarily worsens both training and evaluation loss; Sandwich+GPAS at 1B and the 7B run require gate-gradient clipping. Because stop-gradient overrides the mathematical derivative of the forward scaling, the optimizer is not following the gradient of the displayed forward network alone.

key_findings.claim: Mechanistic measurements are consistent with deeper-layer utilization but do not isolate a unique causal route to downstream gains.
key_findings.evidence: GPAS flattens activation variance, raises gradient and weight norms, and makes layer-ablation scores more uniformly positive. These quantities co-vary under the same trained models; no matched intervention independently holds each factor fixed, and downstream results are single reported runs without uncertainty bars.

method.core_idea: Scale residual-stream activations with learned per-layer gates while using stop-gradient to keep the upstream Jacobian unscaled.
method.mechanism: Insert a scalar-gated subtractive stop-gradient branch after attention and feed-forward residual updates, learn gates jointly during C4 pretraining, and apply the plugin to Pre-LN, DeepNorm, Sandwich-LN, Mix-LN, and layer-norm scaling.
assumptions: Surrogate backward gradients are acceptable even though they are not the exact derivative of the forward network.
Layerwise scalar gates are expressive enough to control variance growth.
Gaussian independence and slowly varying bounded gates used in the gradient analysis approximate trained transformers.
Small-to-midscale C4 improvements predict behavior at larger pretraining scales.

techniques.role: Changes forward activation magnitude while preserving an identity upstream derivative.
Adapts the scaling strength separately for each residual block.
Tests the same intervention across several residual normalization layouts.
Measures whether trained deeper blocks contribute positively to benchmark accuracy.

evaluations.setting: C4 pretraining at 71M, 130M, 250M, 350M, and 1B parameters across five normalization baselines.
evaluations.result: GPAS improves nearly all model/normalization pairs, with 1B gains of 0.24-0.97 perplexity for non-diverged baselines.

evaluations.setting: Commonsense170K fine-tuning of 1B pretrained models and zero-shot evaluation on seven benchmarks.
evaluations.result: Every GPAS variant raises average accuracy; Pre+GPAS gains 2.49 points and LNS+GPAS gains 1.18 points.

evaluations.setting: Partial 7B C4 pretraining for 40K steps/16B tokens.
evaluations.result: Pre+GPAS reaches 13.82 versus 15.27 for Pre-LN at the reported checkpoint.
evaluations.baseline: Matched Pre-LN model with gate-free architecture.

limitations: Author-stated: main systematic experiments stop at 1B parameters, and the 7B run ends far before its planned token budget.
Author-stated: SiLU gates can fluctuate and require clipping; a theoretically safe schedule is unknown.
Author-stated: the method is intended for training from scratch and is unlikely to retrofit cleanly onto existing checkpoints.
Reviewer inference: seed variance, wall-clock overhead, and compute-to-quality efficiency are not reported.
failure_modes: Gate values cross an unstable region and produce loss spikes or divergence.
Surrogate gradients optimize dynamics that do not correspond to any stable forward objective.
Activation scale is reduced while learned weights compensate by growing, erasing numerical or efficiency benefits.
A pretrained checkpoint lacks compatible gates and cannot be converted without substantial retraining.
reusable_insights: Forward signal scale and backward Jacobian scale can be controlled separately with a straight-through construction.
Ablating stop-gradient is essential when attributing gains to gradient preservation rather than simple residual shrinkage.
Layer-removal tests can reveal depth under-utilization that aggregate loss curves miss.
open_questions: Does GPAS improve compute-optimal loss at 7B-70B scale across multiple data mixtures and seeds?
Can an exact-gradient reparameterization reproduce the benefit without a surrogate derivative?
What gate constraints guarantee stability under mixed precision and optimizer-state transients?
Do larger weight norms create quantization, sharpness, or robustness costs after training?

competitive_landscape.title: DeepNet: Scaling Transformers to 1,000 Layers
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepNorm uses analytically chosen residual and initialization scaling to stabilize very deep Post-LN transformers; GPAS learns per-layer forward gates and preserves upstream gradients with stop-gradient.

competitive_landscape.title: Spike No More: Stabilizing the Pre-training of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Spike No More diagnoses and controls loss spikes through initialization/embedding and optimization choices; GPAS directly modifies every residual activation and its backward rule.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers without Normalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Transformers without Normalization replaces normalization with a dynamically stable architecture, whereas GPAS remains a plugin layered onto several normalization schemes.

competitive_landscape.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
competitive_landscape.difference: Xiong et al. explain Pre-LN/Post-LN gradient behavior and warmup needs at initialization; GPAS targets activation accumulation during full pretraining through learned straight-through scaling.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: GPAS is a simple general plugin that preserves gradients while controlling activation variance and consistently accelerates LLM pretraining.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The stop-gradient ablation, five-scale perplexity table, multiple normalization baselines, downstream benchmark table, and partial 7B curve support the empirical claim.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive element is the straight-through residual gate, but scaling and stability claims remain provisional until replicated at full large-model token budgets with exact compute accounting and seed uncertainty.

reviewer_notes: Read all 19 pages, including equations, ablations, theoretical assumptions, partial 7B appendix, and limitations. Competitor records were checked against primary arXiv sources on 2026-08-23.
